info.desc: Revolver is the seventh studio album by English rock band the Beatles, released on 5 August 1966 on the Parlophone label and produced by George Martin. Many of the tracks on Revolver feature an electric guitar-rock sound that contrasts with their previous LP, the folk rock inspired Rubber Soul (1965). In Britain, the fourteen tracks from Revolver were released to radio stations throughout July 1966, "building anticipation for what would clearly be a radical new phase in the group's recording career". It reached number one on both the British chart and American chart and stayed at the top spot for .

podcast.body: An album that incorporated many Indian musical inspirations following The Beatles' visit to India. "un montón de inspiraciones musicales indias que tenemos en el revolver."

srcs.episode: ROSALIA. Por qué la apropiación cultural es un timo.

podcast.body: Released as part of a series of 50th-anniversary collections from 2017 through 2022 by Apple Records. The album was remastered by Giles Martin, son of the original producer George Martin, who deconstructed and reconstructed the album from the original master tapes to achieve a fresher sound with better stereo separation, aiming to sound as close to the original as possible. This box set, priced closer to $100, was particularly revelatory, offering insights like the morose origins of "Yellow Submarine." It is presented as a beautiful object, resembling a vinyl box with a large square shape, and includes a well-written book providing backstory on the band's career at the time. "This may have the most revelatory outtakes."

podcast.body: Released just three months after The Beach Boys' Pet Sounds, Revolver intensified the rivalry between the two bands. Its arrival escalated expectations regarding which group would release "the definitive album of the decade." "Apenas tres meses después, los Beatles respondieron con revolver, intensificando las expectativas sobre quien lanzaría el buen definitivo de la década."

podcast.body: The album *Revolver* preceded *Sgt. Pepper's* and is acknowledged as having initiated a "small revolution" against The Beatles' existing musical style. It paved the way for the greater creative transformations seen in *Sgt. Pepper's*. "esa pequeña revolución en contra de lo que estaban haciendo, ya había empezado un poco antes con el revolver."
